fields.description:
`pyproject.toml:375` omits the `ARG*` family from `select`, so nothing detects a parameter that is
accepted and never read. `ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` reports **72** (56 ARG001, 14 ARG002,
2 ARG005). This backlog concealed three real accepted-then-dropped values, which is the defect class
that motivated this run's unwired-functionality sweep.

**Scope: a one-off sweep. No permanent gate is enabled by this ticket** — see "Revisit" below.

## Classification (a decision procedure covering every violation)

`ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` currently reports **64** (48 ARG001, 14 ARG002, 2 ARG005) —
down from the 72 measured when this ticket was written, because `c61a` ("Retire dead bridge
verbs") landed on `main` and deleted `purge_bridge.py`/`bridge.py`. Rather than a fixed count that
drifts, EVERY violation is dispositioned by the procedure below, applied site-by-site with
`ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` as the completeness oracle. Each of the 64 falls into exactly
one bucket, and each bucket names a concrete action, so no violation is left without a disposition:

1. **Tracked real defect — EXCLUDED, left in place.** An accepted-then-silently-dropped value that
   *should* be consumed is a real bug, tracked separately and NOT fixed in this sweep. Exactly
   three are known: `timeout_s` (`7504-a127-e9b0-42bb`), the discarded close reason
   (`3803-8e04-7c32-4b80`, CLOSED), and the `acli_cmd` bug. Their residual ARG sites —
   `close_precheck.py:166` `_completion_precheck(*, reason)` (keyword-only, body never reads it)
   and `txn.py:189` `force_close_reason` — belong to the close-reason defect's surface; leave the
   violation in place (do not `_`-prefix or `# noqa` it). **If execution surfaces a NEW
   accepted-then-dropped value that looks like a genuine defect, do not fold its fix into this
   sweep:** `create` a ticket, `link <new> fc0c-e218-8b34-4858 discovered_from`, and leave that
   violation in place.
2. **Cluster-1 — reconciler leaf handlers (10 sites), normalize to `**_kwargs`** (see below).
3. **Cluster-2 — `OutboundMapper` Protocol conformance (7 sites), `# noqa: ARG002`** (see below).
4. **Rename UNSAFE (keyword-passed, string-referenced, or keyword-only) — resolve with
   `# noqa: ARG00x` + a one-line reason, never a bare rename.** The parameter is passed by keyword
   at a call site, referenced by string name (`getattr`/`setattr`/`monkeypatch.setattr`/
   `sig.parameters`/`**kwargs` unpacking), or declared keyword-only (after `*`), so `_`-prefixing
   it breaks a caller. Each such site must name the keyword call site or string reference that
   makes it unsafe. (Confirmed example: `_completion_precheck(*, reason)` is keyword-only — but it
   is bucket 1, excluded.)
5. **Interface/Protocol/callback-registry unused, dispatched POSITIONALLY — safe to `_`-prefix.**
   The parameter is pinned by a shared signature (e.g. the eval-scorer registry `case`, the
   reducer `_processors` `event`, the provider-factory `provider_name`, dispatch-table callbacks)
   but unused in this implementation, and every dispatch site calls positionally. `_`-prefix it.
6. **Plain mechanical (SAFE-RENAME) — `_`-prefix the parameter (zero-touch).** No keyword call
   site, no string reference, not keyword-only, not interface-pinned. Where the value is genuinely
   dead and the parameter is purely local, delete the parameter and its call site(s) instead.

The load-bearing safety check is the bucket-4 test: a rename is applied ONLY after confirming with
`grep` (not semantic search alone — Serena omits string references) that the name is neither passed
by keyword nor referenced as a string. The executor records the final per-bucket counts and the
irreducible `# noqa`/excluded total on this ticket (see AC).

### CLUSTER-1 — reconciler leaf handlers (10 violations)

`apply_inbound.py:135,177,205,224` and `apply_outbound.py:92,127,168,190,215`, all dispatched from
`_LEAVES` in `typed_dispatch.py:56-70` and invoked at `:142` as `handler(mutation, **_leaf_kwargs)`.

Two hazards that make a naive rename unsafe:

- `client` is passed **unconditionally** (`typed_dispatch.py:137`: `_leaf_kwargs = {"client": client}`).
  Renaming it to `_client` is an immediate runtime `TypeError`, caught by no type checker.
- `repo_root` is gated by **runtime string introspection** (`typed_dispatch.py:128`:
  `accepts_repo_root = "repo_root" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw`). Renaming flips this to
  `False` and the dispatcher silently stops passing it — a cosmetic lint fix changing dispatch
  behaviour through a string comparison.

**Preferred resolution: normalize the leaves to `**_kwargs`.** This removes all 10 violations
without a rename and decouples dispatch from parameter spelling. Decide once for all ten; do not
rename piecemeal.

**Normalize only the UNUSED parameters — keep the ones the body reads.** "Normalize to
`**_kwargs`" does not mean stripping every named parameter: several leaves DO read `client`
(e.g. `apply_outbound.py` create/conflict) or `repo_root`, and those must stay as explicit named
parameters (keeping them named is itself rename-free and ARG-clean because they are used). The
`**_kwargs` catch-all replaces only the parameters that are accepted-but-unused in that leaf, so
each leaf ends as `def _leaf(mutation, *, client=..., **_kwargs)` or `def _leaf(mutation, **_kwargs)`
depending on what its body actually consumes. The invariant to preserve: every parameter the body
reads is still delivered (the dispatcher passes client unconditionally and repo_root/binding_store
by the string-introspection gate), and every unused one is absorbed by `**_kwargs`.

**Third string-introspected kwarg — `binding_store`.** `typed_dispatch.py` gates a THIRD kwarg by
the identical runtime string check: `accepts_binding_store = "binding_store" in sig.parameters or
_has_var_kw` (`:129`), and per ticket 1577 only leaves that explicitly declare `binding_store`
receive it. Normalizing a leaf to `**_kwargs` sets `_has_var_kw=True`, so `accepts_binding_store`
flips to `True` and EVERY normalized leaf now also receives `binding_store` (and `repo_root`). This
is behaviour-preserving because the leaf body ignores the extra keyword — but it IS a change in
what the dispatcher passes, so it must be pinned by a test (see AC): the observable reconciler
result is identical, and a leaf that previously did not receive `binding_store` still produces the
same events/effects when it now does.

### CLUSTER-2 — `OutboundMapper` Protocol conformance (7 violations)

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:89,90,91,93` and `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py:44,45,46`.
Names are pinned by the Protocol at `_backend.py:370-392`, implemented by two backends, and call
sites pass **by keyword** (`outbound_field_diff.py:285-287,346-348`). Renaming is a contract break
across a Protocol, two backends and two keyword call sites. `suppressed_out`
(`jira_datacenter/backend.py:93`) is documented as accepted-and-ignored on purpose (ticket 8390) and
the Protocol docstring at `_backend.py:379-383` mandates that behaviour.

**Resolution: `# noqa: ARG002` with a Protocol reference.** This is correct code that ARG cannot
model — ruff concedes the general case is blocked on type inference (astral-sh/ruff#15952, open).

## Why no gate

`_`-prefixing is NOT a universally safe remediation here, contrary to a common assumption. Ruff's
lead maintainer, astral-sh/ruff#10409: *"You could change `name: str` to `_name: str`, but that also
carries some risk, since it will break for users that pass keyword arguments."* This codebase proves
it: Cluster-1 renames break runtime dispatch, Cluster-2 renames break keyword call sites.

A survey of ~15 major Python projects found **no project that adopted ARG and later reverted** — but
also that the exclusion is near-universal and always added in the same commit that first enabled
ruff (attrs: `"ARG",  # unused arguments are normal when implementing interfaces`; pythondotorg:
`# Django views/signals/admin methods have required unused args by framework contract`; Home
Assistant: `# generic callbacks and setup methods create a lot of warnings`). Counter-examples exist
and matter: beancount/fava runs ARG fully enabled with no exemptions at all, PlasmaPy for 3+ years.

Enabling ARG here would require carrying roughly **17 permanent inline `# noqa: ARG00x`** — a
discretionary per-site exception mechanism, which this project has ruled against in favour of
restrictions that are absolute or bounded by an invariant. If Cluster-1 is normalized to `**_kwargs`
the irreducible count drops to about 7, which may change that calculus.

## Revisit

Record the irreducible exception count after the sweep. **The next rebar-janitor run must revisit
whether to enable an ARG gate**, using that measured count rather than an estimate. That count and
the revisit note are recorded as a `comment` on THIS ticket (`fc0c-e218-8b34-4858`) — the durable,
queryable home for janitor findings — not in an out-of-tree scratch file. (An earlier draft cited
`.joe-janitor/tools.md`, which does not exist in the repo; the ticket comment supersedes it.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every one of the 64 `ARG` violations is dispositioned by the Classification decision
      procedure — each into exactly one of buckets 1-6, with the bucket-appropriate action applied.
      After the sweep, `ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` reports ONLY the deliberately-retained
      set: the bucket-4 `# noqa`'d sites and the bucket-1 tracked-defect sites (no unclassified
      residual remains).
- [x] Every rename (buckets 5-6) is verified safe against keyword call sites AND against the
      parameter name appearing **as a string** (`getattr`, `setattr`, `monkeypatch.setattr`,
      `sig.parameters`, `**kwargs`), using `grep`, not semantic search alone.
- [x] Every bucket-4 (rename-unsafe) site carries a `# noqa: ARG00x` with a one-line reason that
      names the keyword call site or string reference making a rename unsafe.
- [x] Cluster-1 is resolved by one decision covering all ten leaves; with `**_kwargs`
      normalization, `typed_dispatch.py`'s `accepts_repo_root` introspection still selects the
      right handlers, and a test pins it.
- [x] The `binding_store` side effect of `**_kwargs` normalization is pinned: a test proves that a
      Cluster-1 leaf which (pre-change) did NOT receive `binding_store` now receives it yet
      produces an identical observable result (the extra keyword is inert), so `accepts_binding_store`
      flipping to `True` is behaviour-preserving.
- [x] Cluster-2 carries justified `# noqa: ARG002` referencing the Protocol, or an equivalent that
      does not break the Protocol contract or its keyword call sites.
- [x] The three real defects are NOT folded into this sweep — they remain tracked as
      `7504-a127-e9b0-42bb` (`timeout_s`), `3803-8e04-7c32-4b80` (`close_reason`), and the
      `acli_cmd` bug; any NEW possible-defect surfaced during the sweep is filed as a ticket linked
      `discovered_from fc0c-e218-8b34-4858` and its violation left in place, not fixed here.
- [x] `ARG` is **not** added to `select` in `pyproject.toml` by this ticket.
- [x] The post-sweep per-bucket counts and the irreducible `# noqa`/excluded total are recorded as
      a comment on this ticket.
- [x] No behaviour change: the reconciler dispatch and the outbound mapping produce identical
      results (a test exercises the real dispatch/mapping paths, asserting observable output).
